title: Grain Desk Standing Rule: The Loss Multiplier and What the Member Has Already Delivered
content:
The loss multiplier on a buyout under Grain Marketing Contracts falls with what the member has already delivered against the contract, counting every load standing against it whatever the disposition, because grain in the pit is grain the cooperative no longer has to replace.

- Where the member has delivered at least half the bushels the contract commits and three or more loads stand against it, the multiplier is 0.75.
- Where loads stand against the contract but that pair of conditions is not met, the multiplier is 0.9.
- Where no load stands against the contract, the multiplier is the one the member's marketing programme carries.

## Which loads are counted

Every load standing against the contract, whatever the disposition: a load the member directed to the contract at the scale and a load the member ran straight through to the buyer both count towards the bushels delivered and towards the count of loads.

## The conditions read together

| Net bushels delivered, against the bushels committed | Loads standing | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| at least half | 3 or more | 0.75 |
| at least half | 1 or 2 | 0.9 |
| less than half | 3 or more | 0.9 |
| less than half | 1 or 2 | 0.9 |
| any | none | the multiplier the member's marketing programme carries |

Exactly half the committed bushels satisfies the first condition, and exactly three loads satisfies the second; both must hold together before 0.75 is reached.

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

A contract committing 20,000 bushels carries four loads delivering 11,000 bushels. Both conditions are met, so the multiplier is 0.75, and 9,000 undelivered bushels taken at a hypothetical release rate of 0.20 come to 1,350.00 before the patron release factor. Had two loads delivered those same bushels, the multiplier would be 0.9 and the same bushels would come to 1,620.00.
